findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State an explicit back-out/sequencing plan (e.g. gate deletion on a green typed-only convergence run, or keep a revertable commit boundary) so a post-cutover convergence failure has a defined recovery path.
evidence: Deletion of legacy dispatch is irreversible within the epic
The typed-only convergence proof runs after the compatibility paths are already deleted
T4 requires an explicit rollback/back-out or expand-contract sequencing for destructive steps — acknowledgement alone is insufficient
findings.finding: The plan flips the production route to typed payloads AND deletes the compatibility paths in the same epic, with the typed-only convergence rerun happening AFTER deletion, but states no rollback/back-out path if the post-deletion typed-only convergence fails.
findings.location: Approach: 'flip the one production route to typed payloads/adapters and delete the compatibility paths in the same epic'; 'Rerun a typed-only live convergence/idempotence pass after deletion'
scenarios: Typed-only post-cutover convergence surfaces a defect after legacy dispatch has already been deleted, with no compatibility path to fall back to
findings.suggested_fix: Sequence deletion behind a passing typed-only convergence run, or add: 'Legacy deletion lands as a separate revertable commit gated on the typed-only convergence pass being green.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the rollout/rollback posture for the production flip: whether legacy dispatch is retained for one coexistence window (revertible toggle) before deletion, or justify why a same-epic flip+delete is safe given the parity evidence gate.
evidence: 'After parity, flip the one production route to typed payloads/adapters and delete the compatibility paths in the same epic.'
No flag/canary/staged-rollout mechanism is named for the production flip; deletion is coupled to the flip so rollback-to-legacy requires undoing the deletion.
findings.finding: The plan flips the single production route to typed payloads AND deletes the compatibility dispatch paths within the same epic, but never specifies a staged-rollout or coexistence window, nor a rollback path other than reverting the deletion. Because legacy is removed in the same unit, there is no cheap tested way to fall back to legacy dispatch if the typed route misbehaves post-cutover.
findings.location: Approach: 'flip the one production route to typed payloads/adapters and delete the compatibility paths in the same epic'; AC 'Production no longer converts typed mutations to dictionaries'
scenarios: Typed route ships a regression not caught by the offline corpus or the DC lane; because compat dispatch is already deleted, operators cannot toggle back to legacy and must revert code.
findings.suggested_fix: Sequence the flip and the deletion as two verifiable steps: cut over to typed with the parity + typed-only convergence evidence green, keep compat one commit as a revertible safety net, then delete once the typed-only DC lane is green.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add one concrete motivation for removing the compat dispatch (e.g. the maintenance/ambiguity cost of dual apply() shapes, or a defect the dict round-trip risks) so the deletion's necessity is demonstrated, not just asserted as a completion condition.
evidence: 'Use the portable shadow corpus as the prerequisite... then complete the typed reconciler migration in this story.'
The plan names the legacy mechanism (dict conversion, apply() argument-shape dispatch) to remove but does not state the concrete gap/defect/risk the current dual path causes.
findings.finding: The plan asserts the typed migration should be completed and legacy deleted, but does not concretely motivate why the current dual-dispatch behavior is wrong, insufficient, or costly beyond 'complete the migration' — no named defect, maintenance-burden statement, or reproduction of a problem the dict-conversion/argument-shape dispatch causes.
findings.location: Context / Problem: 'complete the typed reconciler migration in this story. Legacy deletion is a completion condition'
scenarios: A reviewer or implementer cannot tell whether deleting the compat path removes a real hazard/cost or is change-for-its-own-sake, since necessity of removal is asserted, not demonstrated.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'epic' language with the single-ticket structure: either declare this a coherent story (drop 'epic') or, if genuinely an epic, split into children (parity-proof harness entry, production cutover, legacy deletion) with per-child ACs.
evidence: 'flip the one production route... and delete the compatibility paths in the same epic.'
The ticket presents a single flat AC list with no child decomposition, while calling itself an epic.
findings.finding: The plan repeatedly refers to 'the same epic' yet is structured as a single ticket with one flat acceptance-criteria list. If this is an epic, it should have children; if it is one coherent story, the 'epic' framing is misleading. The parity-proof work, the production cutover, and the legacy deletion are argued to be order-dependent (deletion gated on proven parity), which supports keeping them coherent — but the epic-vs-story framing is inconsistent.
findings.location: Approach 'delete the compatibility paths in the same epic'; whole-ticket structure
scenarios: Planning tooling or reviewers treating this as an epic will expect children; treating it as a leaf story will expect it to complete in one coherent unit — the mixed framing creates ambiguity.
